zones.name: Mount Geigerich Area
zones.description: Mount Giegerich is located close to Lemon Pass and is accessed via Griffin Creek. It will take you a few hours to get over to this summit but the views of this area are worth the walk as is the skiing.

zones.name: Hut & access
zones.description: KOKANEE GLACIER PROVINCIAL PARK Kokanee Glacier Provincial Park is renowned as one of the best destinations in western Canada for powder skiing. There is lots of snow and a great variety of runs to choose from including bad-weather tree skiing. A new, state-of-the-art cabin makes Kokanee even more of an attraction. The TS maps for the area are Slocan 82F14 and Kokanee Peak 82F11. The CanadaMapStore maps are Mount Ruppel 082F074 and The Battleship 082F075 ACCESS Kokanee Glacier Cabin is reached by helicopter in winter. The weekly hut rate includes the round-trip helicopter fee. During the winter a custodian is stationed at Kokanee Glacier Cabin. He or she is in contact with the outside world and will provide you with Canadian Avalanche Association forecasts and weather forecasts. A Little History The original Slocan Chief Cabin was built in 1896 for the Smuggler Mining Company, and the mine was in operation as late as 1928. The Kokanee Glacier area was made a provincial park in 1922. In the ear- ly years, the cabin was used regularly by local mountaineering groups but it eventually fell into disrepair. By 1962 BC Parks was considering burning the cabin until a group of local mountaineers, headed by Be1en Butling, spent much of that summer rehabilitating the structure. In 1964 additional repairs were undertaken and for the next ten years the Kootenay Mountaineering Club took care of the cabin. In 1974 the structure was taken over by BC Parks. A new Kokanee Glacier Cabin was built in 2002 and replaced the Slocan Chief Cabin for overnight accommodation. This new cabin was built as a result of campaign efforts carried out in memory of Michel Trudeau and the many other Canadians who have lost their lives while enjoying Canada's back-country. The historic Slocan Chief Cabin is now an interpretive centre. Booking Kokanee Glacier Cabin is now administered by the Alpine Club of Canada. The fee for cabin use is subject to change, so please contact the ACC for the most current rates. The cabin rental also includes helicopter access. There is a lottery system in place to decide which lucky groups get to spend a week skiing in paradise. The ACC can be contacted by phone at 403-678-3200 or by email at info@alpineclubofcanada.com. Their website is www.alpineclubofcanada.com. Hut ● Surrounded by epic terrain & endless views. ● Access to backcountry safety & avalanche information.Beacon Basin. Weather Station with CAA InfoEx ● Hydro Electric, Sewage Treatment, Potable Water, Hot Water. Backup propane & outhouse available. Flush toilets, shower stall with shower bag. ● Full Kitchen with electric & gas stoves, cooking supplies & sinks. Gas fireplace, electric baseboard heaters. ● Comfortable living space with board games and books. ● History Museum: The Slocan Chief ● Caretaker with private quarters. Satellite phone & internet available for emergencies. ● Spacious sleeping quarters provided with sleeping pads. ● Gear drying room with gas fireplace. Communications ACC Staff will have a radio to communicate with the helicopter company on flight days. Staff will also have a satellite phone at the cabin. This phone will be used to get updates on weather and avalanche conditions, and for emergencies only. It is highly recommended that you rent your own satellite phone. This can be done at SK Electronics in Nelson. Phone 250-352-7292 for details. Helicpoter Staging Area and Parking Details You will be meeting at the Kootenay Valley Helicopters hangar on your day of departure. (See the map at the end of this document) The entire group should be at the hangar by 8 a.m. (pacific time) where the pilot will explain the process of the morning’s flights. All of your gear will be weighed at the hangar, and the pilot will give a helicopter safety briefing to the entire group - no one can miss this briefing. Your group will then begin flights from the heliport to the cabin. Kootenay Valley Helicopter’s phone number is 250-505-2150. Each return flight will take about 25 minutes, and your group will be flown in four/five flights. If someone, or a group, misses a flight the cost for an extra flight will be in the neighborhood of $1000. This extra flight would be a cost in addition to the money you have paid for the hut and helicopter. If your group requires an additional flight to get your gear in, these additional flight costs will be payable directly to the helicopter company.

zones.name: Mount John Carter Area
zones.description: Mount John Carter is named for John Carter who worked at Kokanee Glacier Park as a hut custodian and park ranger for many, many years. He also wrote a guide book about the park and died tragically in an avalanche in 1996. Mount John Carter is 2,606 metres high and is connected to Outlook Mountain via a short ridge line.

zones.name: Longer Tours
zones.description: If your energy levels are high, daylight hours long and you are interested in exploring Kokanee Glacier Park then the following two ski tours are ones not to be missed. Both routes take you up the famed Kokanee Glacier (where the park gets its name sake from) and between the Battleship and Mt. Kitchener. From a height of 2,700 metres you get the best views in the park in all directions including East into Coffee Pass, the Sawtooth Ridge and Mount Kane.

zones.name: Mount Nansen Area
zones.description: Mount Nansen is located at the headwaters of Griffin Creek to the Southeast of Kokanee Glacier Cabin. It's summit is a beautiful 1.5 hour walk through a large rolling valley with a modest 360 meter gain.

zones.name: The Pyramid Area
zones.description: The Pyramid is easily viewable from the decks of Kokanee Glacier Cabin by looking Southwest. It's found a few hundred metres down the North ridge of Mount Kitchener and looks like a pyramid from a distance. The Nothwest face offers some good skiing very close to the cabin however the upper routes are often wind scoured by prevailing winds coming North from Kokanee Lake Pass.

zones.name: Mount Robert Smith Area
zones.description: Mount Robert Smith is located Northwest of Kokanee glacier Cabin and accessed via Enterprise Pass and the Enchanted Forest. This is a longer walk and thus a good location to spend the day. The skin back can be relatively long so be sure you are prepared for the day and for weather and conditions to change.

zones.name: Summits & Icefields 2 descents
zones.description: Descents from Summits & Icefields 2. Grid references are UTM zone 11.

zones.name: Tanal Peak Area
zones.description: Tanal Peak is located directly North of Kokanee Glacier Cabin and provides good steep West face skiing on a long sustained pitch that is fairly close to the cabin and easy to access.

routes.name: Molly's Elevens
routes.description: Mount Giegerich summit is 2,249 metres and offers up great views of the West side of Kokanee Glacier Park. The ascent is gentle as is the ski down but be aware of cornices forming on the ridge. To access Mount Giegerich from Kokanee Glacier Cabin head West across Kaslo Lake and skin up the low point which is where Griffin Creek empties into Kaslo Lake. It is a relatively steep 160 meter climb and then things flatten out. Follow this valley as if to ascend Nansen Mountain but instead head more Southwesterly to the peak directly South on the same ridge line. There is a sparsely tree ridge line that you can follow to the summit staying well away of the steeper Skol route on Giegerich's more northerly side. From the summit Molly's Eleven route is the most direct line back down more-or-less the way you ascended. It's a long, mellow heli-ski type route so enjoy. The way back to the cabin is the exact way you came so simply follow your tracks.
routes.notes: Placement: summit = BCGNIS/ATES Mt Giegerich, DEM top 2434 m, not the guide's 2,249 m (the guide's 500 m gain from the cabin fits ~2430 m, so the printed height looks wrong). Skin: across Kaslo Lake to the Griffin Creek mouth on the W shore, the ~165 m climb to ~2125 m, the flat Griffin valley SW to the basin head (~2200 m), S onto the summit's E shoulder (taken as the sparsely treed ridge) and W up it to the top. Descent: back down the shoulder (just N of the skin), into the basin and down Griffin Creek to Kaslo Lake (475 m). All MRDEM-30, so confidence is capped at medium.

routes.name: Mount Giegerich - Skol
routes.description: Mount Giegerich summit is 2,249 metres and offers up great views of the West side of Kokanee Glacier Park. The ascent is gentle as is the ski down but be aware of cornices forming on the ridge. To access Mount Giegerich from Kokanee Glacier Cabin head West across Kaslo Lake and skin up the low point which is where Griffin Creek empties into Kaslo Lake. It is a relatively steep 160 meter climb and then things flatten out. Follow this valley as if to ascend Nansen Mountain but instead head more Southwesterly to the peak directly South on the same ridge line. There is a sparsely tree ridge line that you can follow to the summit staying well away of the steeper Skol route on Giegerich's more northerly side. From the summit Skol is just to the North of the summit and the treed ridge which you likely ascended. Caution is required skiing this route as it is steep and typically Corniced, you will want to ski it one at a time and only in stable conditions. The way back to the Kokanee Glacier Cabin is the exact way you came so simply follow your tracks.
routes.notes: Placement: summit = BCGNIS/ATES Mt Giegerich, DEM top 2434 m, not the guide's 2,249 m (the guide's 500 m gain from the cabin fits ~2430 m, so the printed height looks wrong). Skin: across Kaslo Lake to the Griffin Creek mouth on the W shore, the ~165 m climb to ~2125 m, the flat Griffin valley SW to the basin head (~2200 m), S onto the summit's E shoulder (taken as the sparsely treed ridge) and W up it to the top. Descent (Skol): from the summit ~150 m N along the crest, then NE down the steeper N/NE slope (25-34 deg on MRDEM, steeper in reality) into the Griffin basin at ~2211 m (~225 m). Exact line and cornice not resolvable on MRDEM-30. FLAG: the vertical check is about -55 to -60% against gain_m 500, because that figure is the climb from the cabin, not this face; the return is down the shared skin track (Griffin Creek) to Kaslo Lake, so the line was not stretched to match.

routes.name: Mount Giegerich - East Face
routes.description: Mount Giegerich summit is 2,249 metres and offers up great views of the West side of Kokanee Glacier Park. The ascent is gentle as is the ski down but be aware of cornices forming on the ridge. To access Mount Giegerich from Kokanee Glacier Cabin head West across Kaslo Lake and skin up the low point which is where Griffin Creek empties into Kaslo Lake. It is a relatively steep 160 meter climb and then things flatten out. Follow this valley as if to ascend Nansen Mountain but instead head more Southwesterly to the peak directly South on the same ridge line. There is a sparsely tree ridge line that you can follow to the summit staying well away of the steeper Skol route on Giegerich's more northerly side. From the summit the East face is the large bowl to the south of the treed ridge line you ascended and just south of Molly's Elevens. There is plenty of room on the East Face to ski it lap after lap, the pitch is not steep but it is sustained. The way back to the Kokanee Glacier Cabin is the exact way you came so simply follow your tracks.
routes.notes: Placement: summit = BCGNIS/ATES Mt Giegerich, DEM top 2434 m, not the guide's 2,249 m (the guide's 500 m gain from the cabin fits ~2430 m, so the printed height looks wrong). Skin: across Kaslo Lake to the Griffin Creek mouth on the W shore, the ~165 m climb to ~2125 m, the flat Griffin valley SW to the basin head (~2200 m), S onto the summit's E shoulder (taken as the sparsely treed ridge) and W up it to the top. Descent (East Face): the E-facing slope S of the shoulder, from the summit to the flats at ~2232 m (~200 m, 13-24 deg sustained). The bowl's extent is uncertain on MRDEM-30. FLAG: the vertical check is about -55 to -60% against gain_m 500, because that figure is the climb from the cabin, not this face; the return is down the shared skin track (Griffin Creek) to Kaslo Lake, so the line was not stretched to match.

routes.name: Mount John Carter North
routes.description: Mount John Carter is in full view from Kokanee Glacier Cabin and offers a variety of routes from it's summit at 2,610 metres, they range from long and flowing to short and steep. The most direct approach from Kokanee Glacier Cabin is by crossing Kaslo Lake to the South and skinning up Outlook Creek drainage until you get to Sapphire Lakes. From here you can pick your way up onto the large bench to the East before things cliff out and you get stuck in Glory Basin which only has steep and exposed routes to the summit. Once on the bench you will get a good view of the summit of Mount John Carter off in the distance to the South. It is a long rolling climb to the summit with the last 100 metres being the steepest. Once at the summit take in the 360° views, switch over and ski on a fall line directly back to Kaslo Lake and the cabin.
routes.notes: Placement: skin shares r26's E-shore track to the S end of Kaslo Lake, then follows the shallow Outlook Creek valley W of the Riddles Knob rib to Sapphire Lakes (2262 m), climbs E onto the 2300-2350 m bench and follows the N ridge to the lidar summit (2610 m). Descent drops N from the summit along the ridge/bench and down the rib to r26's finish on the S shore of Kaslo Lake (~650 m). Below ~2500 m both lines run on MRDEM-30 or the lidar/MRDEM blend, so the bench and rib are smoothed.

routes.name: Mount John Carter West #1
routes.description: If you are planning on skinning to the summit of Mount John Carter you may want to consider skiing routes Mount John Carter West #1, #2, or #3. Heck, if you are going that far you may want to ski all three and then still go back to Kokanee Glacier Cabin via the traditional Mount John carter route mentioned above. To access Mount John Carter West #1 you can take the approach talked about above in the Mount John carter North route description or if you like to skin up what you will ski down then follow the Route to Sunset Mountain and instead of heading slightly West to climb Sunset Mountain veer East at the end of Glory Basin. Be warned though, this route is steep and exposed so you better know how the snow pack is behaving before setting out for this route. If snow conditions permit and you are able to ski Mount John Carter West #1 then give #2 or #3 a try or just Yo-yo #1 again and again. All three of these routes are the same aspect on the same ridge but offer their own unique ski experience.
routes.notes: Placement: #1 taken as the southernmost of the three, from the 2570 m knob on the John Carter-Outlook ridge W into the S end of Glory Basin (~2400 m). Skin follows r27's Sunset approach (Griffin Creek, Sapphire Lakes, Glory Basin) and veers E at the basin's end. The face is mostly MRDEM-30, so the steep, exposed terrain is smoothed out; the descent is only ~170 m because the guide's 660 m is the round trip from the cabin (descent_m left null).

routes.name: Mount John Carter West #2
routes.description: If you are planning on skinning to the summit of Mount John Carter you may want to consider skiing routes Mount John Carter West #1, #2, or #3. Heck, if you are going that far you may want to ski all three and then still go back to Kokanee Glacier Cabin via the traditional Mount John carter route mentioned above. To access Mount John Carter West #2 you can take the approach talked about above in the Mount John carter North route description or if you like to skin up what you will ski down then follow the Route to Sunset Mountain and instead of heading slightly West to climb Sunset Mountain veer East near the end of Glory Basin. Be warned though, this route is steep and exposed so you better know how the snow pack is behaving before setting out for this route. If snow conditions permit and you are able to ski Mount John Carter West #2 then give #3 or #1 a try or just Yo-yo #2 again and again. All three of these routes are the same aspect on the same ridge but offer their own unique ski experience.
routes.notes: Placement: #2 taken from the ridge crest ~250 m S of the summit (~2554 m), W into Glory Basin near its S end (~2360 m). Skin = r27's Glory Basin approach, branching E near the end of the basin. The face is mostly MRDEM-30 (crest is lidar/MRDEM blend). The ~195 m descent is far below the 660 m figure, which is the round trip from the cabin (descent_m left null).

routes.name: Mount John Carter West #3
routes.description: If you are planning on skinning to the summit of Mount John Carter you may want to consider skiing routes Mount John Carter West #1, #2, or #3. Heck, if you are going that far you may want to ski all three and then still go back to Kokanee Glacier Cabin via the traditional Mount John carter route mentioned above. To access Mount John Carter West #3 you can take the approach talked about above in the Mount John carter North route description or if you like to skin up what you will ski down then follow the Route to Sunset Mountain and instead of heading slightly West to climb Sunset Mountain veer East well before you get to the end of Glory Basin. Be warned though, this route is steep and exposed so you better know how the snow pack is behaving before setting out for this route. If snow conditions permit and you are able to ski Mount John Carter West #3 then you may want to climb farther South along the ridge to give #2 or #1 a try or just Yo-yo #3 again and again. All three of these routes are the same aspect on the same ridge but offer their own unique ski experience.
routes.notes: Placement: #3 taken as the northernmost line, straight W off the summit (2610 m) into mid Glory Basin (~2325 m), "well before the end". Skin = r27's Glory Basin approach, branching E in mid basin. The alternative r18 approach from the summit is also valid. The face is mostly MRDEM-30. The ~290 m descent is well below the 660 m figure, which is the round trip from the cabin (descent_m left null).

routes.name: Giants Nut Sack
routes.description: The Giants Nut Sack as its called starts just below the summit of Mount John Carter on the more level bench that you can see from Kokanee Glacier Cabin. It ends at the North end of Kokanee Lake and provides a sustained 480 metre descent with some steeper sections and benches. Follow the instructions above in the Mount John Carter North route but instead of climbing the steep 100 metres to the summit switch over and ski down to the East to the North end of Kokanee Lake. Be sure to over shoot the North end of the lake because you don't want to end up in the middle of this giant terrain trap. It is also much steep as you go south down the ridge and avalanche hazard increases. To return to Kokanee glacier Cabin skin through Kokanee Pass and towards Keen Lake and ultimately Kaslo Lake and the cabin. It is a relatively flat and short 2 km skin back to the cabin so you may have time to try other routes along this East facing ridge if the stability allows.
routes.notes: Guide note: Text says 'sustained 480 metre descent' but header gain is 430 m. Placement: starts on the level part of the N ridge just below the summit (~2508 m, where the final steep 100 m begins) and runs NE/E over lidar terrain (cliff bands and benches) to just N of Kokanee Lake's N end, to overshoot the terrain trap (~536 m vs the 480 m in the text; descent_m set from the text). Skin = r18's approach truncated at the bench. The return via Kokanee Pass and Keen Lake is not drawn.

routes.name: Easy's
routes.description: Easy's is on the West face when looking up to Mount John Carter from Kokanee Glacier Cabin. It's a nice sustained line that ends at Kokanee Pass and due to it's 240 descent you can easily ski this line multiple time in the day. From Kokanee glacier Cabin head South across Kalso Lake and then make you way up Keen Creek Drainage avoiding any terrain traps and staying in the relative safety of the trees and not the drainage itself. After climbing to 2,200 metres its time to ski back down. Ski South of the Keen Creek drainage paying close attention to benches and natural hazards. When you get to Kokanee Pass you can either do it again or it's a relatively flat and short 2 km skin back to the cabin.
routes.notes: Placement: Kokanee Pass taken as the DEM saddle between Keen Lake and Kokanee Lake (2021 m, -117.18295 49.75795); the BCGNIS point is ~900 m further S at ~2174 m, on the slope. Top is a 2200-2230 m point on the NE-facing slope SW of the pass, S of Simple Pleasures. Descent ~210 m vs the 240 m in the text; descent_m set from the text. Skin follows the r26 stem to the creek confluence, then Keen Lake's W side and the treed slope. Lower skin is MRDEM-30.

routes.name: Simple Pleasures
routes.description: Simple Pleasures route is just to the North of Easy's but still South of Keen Creek Drainage. It's a nice sustained line that ends at Keen Lake and due to it's 160 metre descent and proximity to Kokanee Glacier Cabin, you can easily get in multiple laps. From Kokanee glacier Cabin head South across Kalso Lake and then make you way up Keen Creek Drainage avoiding any terrain traps and staying in the relative safety of the trees and not the drainage itself. After climbing to 2,160 metres its time to ski back down. Ski South of the Keen Creek drainage paying close attention to benches and natural hazards. When you get to Keen Creek you can either do it again or it's a relatively flat and short 1.5 km skin back to the cabin.
routes.notes: Placement: top is a 2160 m point on the NE-facing slope SW of Keen Lake, between Easy's (S) and Beaujolais (N), with the descent ending at Keen Lake's S shore (~190 m vs 160 m stated; descent_m set from the text). Skin follows the r26 stem, then Keen Lake's W side. All MRDEM-30, so the benches are smoothed and the position is a guess.

routes.name: Beaujolais
routes.description: Beaujolais is the most Northerly route in the East facing chain of Giant's Nut Sack, Easy's and Simple Pleasures and offers just over 200 metres of good close to the cabin skiing. From Kokanee glacier Cabin head South across Kalso Lake and then make you way up Keen Creek Drainage avoiding any terrain traps and staying in the relative safety of the trees and not the drainage itself. When the terrain starts to mellow out just over 2,200 metres its time to de-skin and ski down almost the way you came up and with Keen Lake in your sights. it's a relatively flat and short 1 km skin back to the cabin.
routes.notes: Placement: "just over 2,200 m" taken where the Riddles Knob rib meets the mellower bench (~2226 m, S of r26's top). Skin reuses all of r26's skin to Riddles Knob, then continues up the rib. Descent goes NNE down the rib's E flank, "almost the way you came up", to the Commission/Keen flats ~1 km from the cabin (~240 m; descent_m 200 from "just over 200 metres"). All MRDEM-30, so confidence is low and the line lies close to r24 and r26.

routes.name: Cat Fish Comes Home
routes.description: This route is very close to the cabin and lightly treed with many variations to ski. Be sure to lay down good lines as they will be on full display from those at Kokanee Glacier Cabin. Head to the South end of Kaslo Lake from Kokanee Glacier Cabin and start climbing the treed rib between Commission Creek and Outlook Creek. The top is called Riddles Knob and stands at 2160 metres. The ski down is through sparse trees and rolling terrain with a few benches thrown in to keep you alert. After 260 metres you will be back at the shores of Kaslo Lake with the Cabin in sight.
routes.notes: Placement: Riddles Knob taken as the 2160 m point (DEM 2158-2161 m) on the NNE rib that ends at the Commission/Outlook creek confluence S of Kaslo Lake; skin follows the E shore of Kaslo Lake to its S end, then the rib crest. Descent runs N down the rib's NW flank to the S shore of Kaslo Lake (~200 m on the DEM vs the 260 m stated; descent_m set from "After 260 metres"). Area is MRDEM-30 only, so benches and the knob itself are smoothed.

routes.name: Sunset Mountain
routes.description: Sunset mountain is due south of Sapphire Lakes at the end of Glory Basin and a nice climb with a sustained fall line of over 210 metres. This slope gets cooked by the sun in late winter as it is East facing so best to get there early if you plan to skin to the top. The approach from Kokanee Glacier Cabin is to follow the general direction of the summer trail to Sapphire Lakes. Cross Kaslo Lake and head West up Griffin Creek, then South to Sapphire Lakes. Continue on to Glory Basin and you will see Sunset Mountain at the end of the valley. It's a long haul to get to Sunset so while you are there you may want to consider skiing Mount John Carter as well.
routes.notes: Placement: summit from the DEM (2578 m, near the BCGNIS point at the S end of Glory Basin); descent follows the NE/E-facing fall line ~220 m to the basin floor (descent_m 210 from "over 210 metres"). Skin crosses Kaslo Lake to the Griffin Creek mouth, goes W up Griffin Creek, S to Sapphire Lakes and up Glory Basin. The whole route is MRDEM-30, so the face detail is smoothed.

routes.name: Andy's Slide
routes.description: Andy's Slide is a short but sweet route that dumps into the Commission Creek drainage at the North end of Mount John Carter. It is only 100m but its steep and cliffy. As the name suggests this North facing slope is prone to slides so be sure to pick your days when conditions are stable. There are plenty of variations in this mini bowl feature so poke around and ski a few but be sure to be cautious. From Kokanee Glacier Cabin head Southeast across Kaslo Lake and head to the end of Commission Creek drainage, there you will see Andy's Slide, it's that simple. To head home just go back the way you came.
routes.notes: Placement: taken as the ~110 m N/NNE-facing steep pitch (lidar, 27-43 deg) at the head of the drainage that runs N from the north end of Mount John Carter, ~2320 to ~2210 m (descent_m 100 from "only 100m"). The creek naming is uncertain: BCGNIS puts the Commission and Outlook Creek mouths at the same point, and on the DEM this bowl partly drains toward Kokanee Lake. Skin follows the r26 stem, then goes S up the drainage. Return is the same way.

routes.name: The Keyhole
routes.description: Mark's Slot can be found on the North Face of Mt. Robert Smith so follow the directions for that route in order to gain the saddle below and to the East of the summit. Once at the saddle the descent is pretty obvious, you ski down the North face descending to valley bottom. Be aware of cornices on the ridge as they are common as is wind loading just over the ridge as you drop in. There are plenty of lines on this North aspect so you can skin back to the top to try other options or head East from the valley floor trending Southeast to arrive at Tanal Lake and Enterprise Pass. There is huge exposure from both sides once at Tanal Lake and from the West face of Tanal Peak so be sure to stay well away from this face and in the trees. From Tanal Lake the ascent is a moderate 200 metre ski up. Once you reach the pass Kokanee Glacier Cabin is to the East via the heli-pad.
routes.notes:
Guide note: SOURCE ERROR: description text is a copy of #8 Mark's Slot; approach/descent for The Keyhole is undocumented. ATES has a 'Keyhole' landmark at -117.152373, 49.749477 (between Esmeralda Peak and Kokanee Glacier).

Placement: the guide text is a copy of #8 Mark's Slot, so this line is inferred. Skin follows the zone intro: cabin, Kaslo Lake E shore (same coordinates as #26), Keen Lake, then E up between the Battleship and Mt Kitchener onto the Kokanee Glacier and SE across it to the floor of the ATES 'Keyhole' notch (~2713 m, ~70 m SE of the ATES point, between Giants Kneecap and Esmeralda Peak). That is ~760 m of gain, plus ~60 m for the return over the Kokanee Lake/Keen Lake col: close to the guide's 800 m. Descent assumed to go W through the Keyhole along the lowest-angle corridor (least-slope path on the DEM: notch floor, then the bowl trending SW) to the SE shore of Kokanee Lake (~750 m), returning N past Keen Lake to the cabin (not drawn). Low confidence: the direction of travel and the descent side are guesses. QA fix: the skin climb from Keen Lake to just S of the Battleship was re-routed along a least-slope DEM path (swinging ~300-600 m N of the old straight line) to avoid a 71 deg lidar rock step, so terrain under the skin now stays below 38 deg (the new stretch is on 30 m MRDEM data, so small steps may be smoothed out).

routes.name: Gray's Peak
routes.description: Gray's Peak is the ultimate big objective from Kokanee Glacier Cabin as takes a full day and lots of energy to complete as this is one of the highest peaks in the park. You will traverse Kokanee Glacier from its North end to to its South and get views of near-by Nelson from the 2,753 metre summit. You will cover approximately 22 kilometres round trip and reach the Southern boundary of the park crossing significant glaciated terrain so prepare accordingly and ensure you have enough skill, good weather and solid conditions. To reach the summit of Gray's Peak follow the directions to The Keyhole found above but continue on past Cond Peak (2,801) metres) and Kokanee Peak (2,790 metres). Once past Kokanee Peak you will get your first glimpse of Gray's Peak in the distance to the far South. After a brief descent of a few hundred metres you will end up at the saddle of Kokanee Peak and Gray's Peak, mark this spot as this is where you will descend heading West once you summit Gray's Peak itself. From here continue climbing another 220 metre to gain the summit of Gray's Peak. The last 15 metres is very steep and slightly exposed so you may want to boot pack this portions if conditions permit. The route down is by skiing back to the saddle we spoke of earlier. Ski down the West face contouring North as you go. Be careful not to ski lower than 2,000 meter elevation as you need to gain Kokanee Lake at this elevation. The terrain is very benchy and rolling so the ski tour back home is not as straight forward as you may think. This Tour will take a full day so leave early and be very well prepared.
routes.notes:
Guide note: Refers to The Keyhole directions, which are missing (see r34).

Placement: skin reuses r34's skin coordinates from the cabin onto Kokanee Glacier (to ~350 m short of the Keyhole), then a least-cost DEM path SE up the glacier past the NE sides of Cond Peak and Kokanee Peak (~2750 m), down ~210 m to the Kokanee Peak - Gray's Peak saddle (DEM 2539 m, exactly 220 m below the 2759 m lidar summit, as the guide says) and up the ridge to the summit; the last ~15 m is steep (boot pack, as stated). Descent goes back to the saddle, then down the West face contouring NW above 2000 m to the S end of Kokanee Lake (same end point as r34's descent; ~790 m vertical); two short cliff bands on the face were routed around on the 2 m grid. The return from Kokanee Lake to the cabin (N past Keen Lake) is not drawn. The descent and the new skin section are on lidar, but the skin as a whole is ~62% 30 m MRDEM (the shared approach), and the approach itself is inferred because the Keyhole directions are missing, so confidence is medium.

routes.name: Northern Exposure
routes.description: From Kokanee Glacier Cabin put your skins on and head West across Kaslo Lake and skin up the low point which is where Griffin Creek empties into Kaslo Lake. It is a relatively steep 160 meter climb and then things flatten out. Follow this valley gently contouring up to the ridge to the North (your right) and head due West. This climb should be gentle as you are only gaining 100 meters over the next kilometre. Once on the ridge you can drop into the lower 3/4 of Northern Exposure by switching to ski mode before the last steep climb to the false summit you see from the ridge or climb to this summit and get an extra 120 metres of skiing. The climb to the summit is steep, expose alpine so be sure that current avi conditions permit this addition to the ski before you attempt to climb higher. The ski down is 340 metres of steep, open rolly skiing so be cautious. Ski to the valley floor and find a safe place to put your skins on. You can skin back up the way you skied down more or less and do it again however it is steep and exposed in this area. The common route is to ski down through the Enchanted Forest loosing minimal elevation as you go. You will head Southeast and gain Enterprise Pass in order to get back to Kaslo Lake and Kokanee Glacier Cabin from where you started.
routes.notes: Placement: Read the 'false summit' as Nansen's N summit (2433 m) at the W end of the NE ridge: summit to ridge is ~115 m (guide 120) and summit to the basin floor N of the ridge is ~345 m (guide 340), a good numeric fit. The descent runs NE down the N face to the basin floor (~2088 m). Shared approach (identical coords on r09-r14 to the Griffin bench, r09-r13 to the Nansen N summit): cabin, across Kaslo Lake to the Griffin Creek mouth (W shore), up the ~170 m step to the Griffin bench (~2125 m), NW onto the knoll and due W along Nansen's NE ridge (~2310 m flat), then the steep ~110 m to Nansen's N summit (~2433 m MRDEM). MRDEM skin gain is ~490 m vs guide 360. Return via the Enchanted Forest and Enterprise Pass is not drawn. Terrain is MRDEM-30 only (quality 3), so gullies, benches and cornices are not resolved.

routes.name: Roll Map
routes.description: From Kokanee Glacier Cabin put your skins on and head West across Kaslo Lake and skin up the low point which is where Griffin Creek empties into Kaslo Lake. It is a relatively steep 160 meter climb and then things flatten out. Follow this valley gently contouring up to the ridge to the North (your right) and head due West. This climb should be gentle as you are only gaining 100 meters over the next kilometre. Once on the ridge continue skinning West along the ridge and climb the prominent peak at the end of the ridge. This steep 100 meter climb to the summit has no trees and can be dangerous if conditions are not ideal so ensure you have the skills and your timing is right. Once on the summit ridge continue past the summit and descend around the small cliff band to gain access to Roll Map. The ski down is 200 metres, open and benchy so pick your line from the top and avoid obvious hazards. Ski to the valley floor and find a safe place to put your skins on. You can ski East down the valley 500 meters and then climb back to the ridge to do it again however it is steep and exposed in this area. The common route is to ski down through the Enchanted Forest loosing minimal elevation as you go. You will head Southeast and gain Enterprise Pass in order to get back to Kaslo Lake and Kokanee Glacier Cabin from where you started.
routes.notes: Placement: Start at the dip just W of Nansen's N summit ('past the summit, around the small cliff band') and ski N ~200 m into the W end of the basin. Exact entry is a guess. Shared approach (identical coords on r09-r14 to the Griffin bench, r09-r13 to the Nansen N summit): cabin, across Kaslo Lake to the Griffin Creek mouth (W shore), up the ~170 m step to the Griffin bench (~2125 m), NW onto the knoll and due W along Nansen's NE ridge (~2310 m flat), then the steep ~110 m to Nansen's N summit (~2433 m MRDEM). Return via the Enchanted Forest and Enterprise Pass is not drawn. Terrain is MRDEM-30 only (quality 3), so gullies, benches and cornices are not resolved.

routes.name: Aquavit
routes.description: Aquavit is the next run to the West of Roll Map so from Kokanee Glacier Cabin head West across Kaslo Lake and skin up the low point which is where Griffin Creek empties into Kaslo Lake. It is a relatively steep 160 meter climb and then things flatten out. Follow this valley gently contouring up to the ridge to the North (your right) and head due West. This climb should be gentle as you are only gaining 100 meters over the next kilometre. Once on the ridge continue skinning West along the ridge and climb the prominent peak at the end of the ridge. This steep 100 meter climb to the summit has no trees and can be dangerous if conditions are not ideal so ensure you have the skills and your timing is right. Once on the summit ridge continue past the summit and descend around the small cliff band and skin up the ridge about half way to the next peak. The ski down is 200 metres, open and benchy so pick your line from the top and avoid obvious hazards. Ski to the valley floor and find a safe place to put your skins on. You can ski East down the valley 500 meters and then climb back to the ridge to do it again however it is steep and exposed in this area. The common route is to ski down through the Enchanted Forest loosing minimal elevation as you go. You will head Southeast and gain Enterprise Pass in order to get back to Kaslo Lake and Kokanee Glacier Cabin from where you started.
routes.notes: Placement: 'Halfway to the next peak' read as the col (~2364 m) on the ridge NW from the N summit toward the 2370 m bump; skis NE ~200 m into the basin. Could equally be one gully either side. Shared approach (identical coords on r09-r14 to the Griffin bench, r09-r13 to the Nansen N summit): cabin, across Kaslo Lake to the Griffin Creek mouth (W shore), up the ~170 m step to the Griffin bench (~2125 m), NW onto the knoll and due W along Nansen's NE ridge (~2310 m flat), then the steep ~110 m to Nansen's N summit (~2433 m MRDEM). Return via the Enchanted Forest and Enterprise Pass is not drawn. Terrain is MRDEM-30 only (quality 3), so gullies, benches and cornices are not resolved.

routes.name: Lute Fish
routes.description: Lute Fish is the second run to the West of Roll Map so from Kokanee Glacier Cabin head West across Kaslo Lake and skin up the low point which is where Griffin Creek empties into Kaslo Lake. It is a relatively steep 160 meter climb and then things flatten out. Follow this valley gently contouring up to the ridge to the North (your right) and head due West. This climb should be gentle as you are only gaining 100 meters over the next kilometre. Once on the ridge continue skinning West along the ridge and climb the prominent peak at the end of the ridge. This steep 100 meter climb to the summit has no trees and can be dangerous if conditions are not ideal so ensure you have the skills and your timing is right. Once on the summit ridge continue past the summit and descend around the small cliff band and skin up the ridge stopping just before it gets steep and corniced . The ski down is 280 metres, open, steep and rolly so pick your line from the top and avoid obvious hazards. Ski to the valley floor and find a safe place to put your skins on. You can ski East down the valley 600 meters and then climb back to the ridge to do it again however it is steep and exposed in this area. The common route is to ski down through the Enchanted Forest loosing minimal elevation as you go. You will head Southeast and gain Enterprise Pass in order to get back to Kaslo Lake and Kokanee Glacier Cabin from where you started.
routes.notes: Placement: Start just below the 2370 m bump NW of the N summit ('before it gets steep and corniced'); skis E/NE ~275 m to the basin floor. Guide gain 450 is not matched by MRDEM relative heights. Shared approach (identical coords on r09-r14 to the Griffin bench, r09-r13 to the Nansen N summit): cabin, across Kaslo Lake to the Griffin Creek mouth (W shore), up the ~170 m step to the Griffin bench (~2125 m), NW onto the knoll and due W along Nansen's NE ridge (~2310 m flat), then the steep ~110 m to Nansen's N summit (~2433 m MRDEM). Return via the Enchanted Forest and Enterprise Pass is not drawn. Terrain is MRDEM-30 only (quality 3), so gullies, benches and cornices are not resolved.

routes.name: Unibomber
routes.description: Unibomber is the last route on the same ridge as Aquavit so its access is the same. From Kokanee Glacier Cabin head West across Kaslo Lake and skin up the low point which is where Griffin Creek empties into Kaslo Lake. It's a relatively steep 160 meter climb and then things flatten out. Follow this valley gently contouring up to the ridge to the North (your right) and head due West. This climb should be gentle as you are only gaining 100 meters over the next kilometre. Once on the ridge continue skinning West along the ridge and climb the prominent peak at the end of the ridge. This steep 100 meter climb to the summit has no trees and can be dangerous if conditions are not ideal so ensure you have the skills and your timing is right. Once on the summit ridge continue past the summit and descend around the small cliff band and continue climbing the mellow ridge line. As things steepen stay well back from cornices that tend to form on the North aspect of the ridge. You will once again top out on a peak and then descend slightly to gain access to Unibomber. You may find cornices at the entrance to this run so caution is required. The ski down is 300 metres, open, steep and exposed so ensure you have good stability before dropping in. Ski to the valley floor and find a safe place to put your skins on. You can ski East down the valley 700 meters and then climb back to the ridge to do it again however it is steep and exposed in this area. The common route is to ski down through the Enchanted Forest loosing minimal elevation as you go. You will head Southeast and gain Enterprise Pass in order to get back to Kaslo Lake and Kokanee Glacier Cabin from where you started.
routes.notes: Placement: 'Top out on a peak' read as the 2370 m bump on the ridge running N from Nansen toward Mt Robert Smith; entry just N of it, skis E/NE ~270 m (guide 300) down the N side of the basin. If the intended peak is Robert Smith (2413 m) this line moves ~600 m N. Shared approach (identical coords on r09-r14 to the Griffin bench, r09-r13 to the Nansen N summit): cabin, across Kaslo Lake to the Griffin Creek mouth (W shore), up the ~170 m step to the Griffin bench (~2125 m), NW onto the knoll and due W along Nansen's NE ridge (~2310 m flat), then the steep ~110 m to Nansen's N summit (~2433 m MRDEM). Return via the Enchanted Forest and Enterprise Pass is not drawn. Terrain is MRDEM-30 only (quality 3), so gullies, benches and cornices are not resolved.

routes.name: Nansen East Face
routes.description: Mount Nansen is due West of Kokanee glacier Cabin so from Kokanee Glacier Cabin head West across Kaslo Lake and skin up the low point which is where Griffin Creek empties into Kaslo Lake. It is a relatively steep 160 meter climb and then things flatten out. Follow this valley to its Westerly terminus skirting around micro features and heading South following Griffen Creek and then contouring back to the Northwest when the terrain steepens. Here you will see Mount Nansen in the distance with a further 260 metre climb required on steep open slopes so be sure stability and skills of the group are in your favour. Ski down the way you came and repeat or head back to the cabin.
routes.notes: Placement: Summit 2448 m (MRDEM, terrain_probe near BCGNIS Nansen Mountain); skin follows the Griffin valley S then contours NW, last ~250 m on open E-facing slopes (guide 260); skin gain ~500 m matches the guide. Descent is the E face, then 'the way you came' down Griffin to the Kaslo Lake shore (~490 m). Shares cabin-to-Griffin-bench coords with r09-r13. Terrain is MRDEM-30 only (quality 3), so gullies, benches and cornices are not resolved.

routes.name: Field of Dreams
routes.description: Fields of Dreams is the closest route to Kokanee Glacier Cabin listed in this section. It provides a quick lap with good pitch in open alpine terrain. From Kokanee glacier Cabin follow the summer trail to the Slocan Chief Cabin but once you reach the highpoint, instead of descending down into the Kalmia Lake area stay on the ridge and continue climbing Southeast up Smuggler's Ridge. After a short one kilometer skin you will be at the starting point of Field of Dreams. Ski down amongst the sparse trees avoiding any steeper sections and cliff bands. At the bottom of the valley you should be standing beside Keen Lake and from here it's a short, flat skin back to Kaslo Lake and Kokanee Glacier Cabin.
routes.notes: Placement: Start on Smuggler's Ridge at the ATES 'Smugglers Ridge' point (~2250 m, ~0.9 km SE of the 2055 m knob between Kaslo and Kalmia lakes, taken as the trail highpoint); descent drops WSW (aspect ~250 deg) through the 'Sunny Smugglers' slope to the E shore of Keen Lake (~1975 m), 273 m. Skin: cabin -> knob -> SE along the ridge crest (least-cost path). Entirely on MRDEM-30 (no lidar), so cliff bands are not resolved. The zone intro's 'looking Southwest' from the cabin is wrong: the Pyramid is SE of the cabin.

routes.name: J.C.'s
routes.description: J.C.'s starting point is just South of Field of Dreams so the access is the same. Again you will climb Southeast up Smuggler's Ridge and after a short skin you will be at the starting point of J.C.'s. Ski down amongst the sparse trees avoiding any steeper sections and cliff bands. At the bottom of the valley you will only be a short distance to Keen Lake and from here it's a short, flat skin back to Kaslo Lake and Kokanee Glacier Cabin.
routes.notes: Placement: Start ~130 m S of Field of Dreams' start (~2260 m); descent W/WSW down the face to the valley floor just S of Keen Lake (~1985 m), 276 m. Skin = Field of Dreams skin plus a short step S. 'Just South' is vague; entirely on MRDEM-30.

routes.name: Knee D-2
routes.description: Knee D-2 is a route that starts just below the Pyramid and leads directly into J.C's to provide a much longer ski descent than the previous two routes mentioned. To access Knee D-2 again climb Southeast up Smuggler's Ridge, this time skin higher up to 2,400 metres just below The Pyramid. Caution is required as the terrain is open and gradually gets steeper as you skin higher. Ski down with caution eventually reaching the start of J.C.'s and continue skiing amongst the sparse trees avoiding any steeper sections and cliff bands. At the bottom of the valley you will only be a short distance to Keen Lake and from here it's a short, flat skin back to Kaslo Lake and Kokanee Glacier Cabin.
routes.notes: Placement: Start at 2400 m on the NW-facing slope just NW (below) of the Pyramid, taken as the N-ridge nose of Mt Kitchener at ~487780/5511920 UTM (~2475 m; no distinct knob in the DEM); descent NW/W into the start of J.C.'s, then J.C.'s line to near Keen Lake, 415 m. Skin continues SE up the slope from Field of Dreams' start. 100% MRDEM-30.

routes.name: Knee Dropping Tree Fairy
routes.description: Knee Dropping Tree Fairy is a much longer run as it starts just above and to the South of The Pyramid with a descent of 540 metres when you include Field of Dreams which this route leads right into. The access from Kokanee Glacier Cabin is again via Smuggler's Ridge, this time skin higher up to 2,500 metres. Caution is required as the terrain is open, typically wind swept and gradually gets steeper as you skin higher. Ski down with caution eventually reaching Field of Dreams and continue skiing amongst the sparse trees avoiding any steeper sections and cliff bands. At the bottom of the valley you will only be standing next to Keen Lake and from here it's a short, flat skin back to Kaslo Lake and Kokanee Glacier Cabin.
routes.notes: Placement: Start at ~2505 m on Kitchener's N ridge just S of (above) the assumed Pyramid; descent down the NW face (aspect ~330 deg) into Field of Dreams' start, then Field of Dreams to Keen Lake, 532 m (guide 540). Skin shares r31's and continues to 2500 m. Pyramid location is uncertain; ~85% MRDEM-30, top in the lidar/MRDEM blend.

routes.name: Squat to Pee
routes.description: Squat to pee is a short but steep route which is located on the ridge between The Pyramid and Mt. Kitchener. It only provides 140 metres of skiing but from its terminus you can then ski Knee Dropping Tree Fairy and then Filed of Dreams for the full 660m metre descent. The upper reaches of the Pyramid are steep and typically wind scoured so caution and good avi senses are required. At the bottom of the valley you will only be close to Keen Lake depending upon if you skied Field of Dreams or J.C.'s. From here it's a short, flat skin back to Kaslo Lake and Kokanee Glacier Cabin.
routes.notes: Guide note: Text says 'Filed of Dreams' (= Field of Dreams). Placement: Squat to Pee proper is the top ~145 m: from ~2655 m on the crest of Kitchener's N ridge (lidar, ~25 deg at the start; brief 45 deg step) down the ridge's W side to Knee Dropping Tree Fairy's start (~2505 m); the line continues through KDTF and Field of Dreams to Keen Lake, 680 m total (text says 660). Skin extends r32's up the crest (steep top, may need booting). ~71% MRDEM-30, 27% blend.

routes.name: Mount Robert Smith Southeast Face
routes.description: Mount Robert Smith is a fun objective from Kokanee Glacier Cabin which provides a pretty straight forward 340 metre descent. Access is either via skiing Unibomber, Lute Fish, Aquavit or Roll Map as mentioned below or the more common and faster route of skinning through Enterprise Pass. Here we will describe the Enterprise Pass route. From Kokanee glacier Cabin head Northwest to the obvious pass behind the cabin and heli-pad. It's a short 60 metre climb to gain the pass and once through you will begin to descend to the what's know as "The Enchanted Forest". Descend only about 20 meters and then start contouring dead west so that you do not loose too much elevation that you will ultimately have to skin back up. Heading West you will enter the trees of the Enchanted Forest and after approximately one kilometre you will emerge in an open value with the routes Unibomber, Lute Fish, Aquavit and Roll Map on your left and the big beautiful Southeast face of Mt. Robert Smith on your right. There are plenty or routes up the face so pick the safest line and be sure to use the few islands of safety. The typical route is to gain the saddle between Mount Robert Smith and the unknown peak to the East. From the saddle the summit is only a short distance away. Be sure avi conditions permit this ascent/descent as do your skills and judgement. Once on the summit the ski down offers plenty of room for everyone and lots of variations. From the valley floor use your up track again or retrace your skin track back to Kokanee glacier Cabin.
routes.notes: Placement: summit = BCGNIS Mt Robert Smith (DEM 2413 m; a higher 2441 m point lies ~650 m NW). Skin: cabin, heli-pad, Enterprise Pass (~2016 m), then a traverse W at ~1980-2000 m per the guide (MRDEM shows 35-40 deg sidehill on the N flank of the knoll W of the pass; the real line is in the Enchanted Forest trees), up the open valley to ~2080 m, then the SE face (20-33 deg on MRDEM) to the 2331 m saddle E of the summit. Then the ridge W to the summit. Descent: SE fall line from the summit to the valley floor at ~2073 m, giving the guide's stated 340 m (descent_m set to 340). All MRDEM-30, so confidence is capped at medium.

routes.name: Mark's Slot
routes.description: Mark's Slot can be found on the North Face of Mt. Robert Smith so follow the directions for that route in order to gain the saddle below and to the East of the summit. Once at the saddle the descent is pretty obvious, you ski down the North face descending to valley bottom. Be aware of cornices on the ridge as they are common as is wind loading just over the ridge as you drop in. There are plenty of lines on this North aspect so you can skin back to the top to try other options or head East from the valley floor trending Southeast to arrive at Tanal Lake and Enterprise Pass. There is huge exposure from both sides once at Tanal Lake and from the West face of Tanal Peak so be sure to stay well away from this face and in the trees. From Tanal Lake the ascent is a moderate 200 metre ski up. Once you reach the pass Kokanee Glacier Cabin is to the East via the heli-pad.
routes.notes: Placement: skin identical to r07 up to the saddle. Summit = BCGNIS Mt Robert Smith (DEM 2413 m; a higher 2441 m point lies ~650 m NW). Route: cabin, heli-pad, Enterprise Pass (~2016 m), then a traverse W at ~1980-2000 m per the guide (MRDEM shows 35-40 deg sidehill on the N flank of the knoll W of the pass; the real line is in the Enchanted Forest trees), up the open valley to ~2080 m, then the SE face (20-33 deg on MRDEM) to the 2331 m saddle E of the summit. Descent: N off the saddle down the N face to the valley floor at ~1940 m (390 m). The slot itself can't be resolved on MRDEM-30, so confidence is low. Exit not drawn: valley floor E/SE to Tanal Lake (~1790 m), ~225 m up to Enterprise Pass, then E via the heli-pad.

routes.name: Battleship NW slope
routes.description: The large northwest-facing slope below The Battleship (488200 E 5511800 ) and The Giant's Kneecap (488700 E 5511400 N) down toward the Slocan Chief Cabin gives an excellent run of about 600 vertical metres.
routes.notes: Placement: starts at the printed Battleship ref (488200/5511800, about 2590 m) and runs NW down the slope between the Battleship spur and Smuggler's Ridge to Kalmia Lake (about 2000 m), toward the Slocan Chief Cabin; DEM vertical 591 m vs 600. All on MRDEM 30 m, so the exact fall line is smoothed. Skin shares si5's Smuggler's Ridge track, then traverses to the start.

routes.name: Esmeralda to Joker Lakes
routes.description: One of the finest runs is to ski north from the summit of Esmeralda or Cond peak down Kokanee Glacier to an unnamed lake (489700 E 5512400 N), then farther down to Joker Lakes (490100 E 5513300 N).This is a long run, about 800 vertical metres.
routes.notes: Placement: from Cond Peak summit (lidar, 2803 m) N down Kokanee Glacier through the printed unnamed-lake ref (489700/5512400) to the printed Joker Lakes ref (490100/5513300, about 2004 m); DEM vertical 799 m vs 800. Mostly MRDEM 30 m. Skin is interpretive: si1's track up Smuggler's Ridge to the Battleship, then S of the Giant's Kneecap across the upper glacier to Cond.

routes.name: Outlook Mountain north summit
routes.description: Another good run can be had from the north summit of Outlook Mountain (486200 E 5509800 N). Head north, then curve down to the right to reach Kokanee Pass (s50 vertical metres). The approach to this peak is up Outlook Creek to Lemon Pass, where the way above is blocked by a short steep section. It is possible to ascend the obstacle by a narrow crest just above Lemon Pass (485100 E 55113°0 N).
routes.notes: Guide note: si3 'north summit of Outlook Mountain (486200 E 5509800 N)' coincides with today's Mount John Carter (ATES landmark within ~60 m). 's50 vertical metres' is a typo (likely 550 or 650). '55113°0' = 5511300; '55II300' = 5511300. Placement: from Mount John Carter summit (= the printed north summit of Outlook, lidar 2609 m) N along the crest, then right (NE) to Kokanee Pass taken as the DEM low point between Kokanee and Keen lakes (486805/5511705, 2026 m); the BCGNIS pass point sits 870 m S on a 46 deg slope, so it was not used. Vertical 583 m fits 's50' read as 550. Skin crosses Kaslo Lake, goes up Outlook Creek to the printed crest ref (485100/5511300, unreliable) and follows the ridge SE to the summit; the BCGNIS Lemon Pass is 900 m W and lower, so S&I's 'Lemon Pass' is assumed to be the col by Sapphire Lakes.

routes.name: Nansen and Giegerich crests
routes.description: Good runs of about 250 vertical metres can be found from the crests of Nansen Mountain and Mount Giegerich into the basin of Griffith Creek.
routes.notes: Placement: one representative line from the Nansen crest summit (2448 m) E/NE into the Griffin Creek basin (about 2185 m); DEM vertical 262 m vs 250. The guide names no specific line, and Giegerich's E side into the same basin is an equal alternative. All MRDEM 30 m.

routes.name: Smuggler's Ridge west flank
routes.description: If the weather is overcast, a good location for skiing with a few trees to enhance visibility is along the west flank of Smuggler's Ridge and, near the bottom, below the ridge toward Slocan Chief Cabin. Smuggler's Ridge is the crest which descends northwest from The Pyramids (488200 E 55II300 N) to about 486600 E 5512600 .
routes.notes: Placement: Smuggler's Ridge from the printed refs (Pyramids 488200/5511300 to 486600/5512600). Descent drops off the crest at about 2460 m down the W flank, then runs NW along the foot of the ridge toward Kaslo Lake and the Slocan Chief Cabin (1975 m, 483 m vertical). The flank is broad, so this is one representative line. Mostly MRDEM 30 m. Skin climbs the ridge's NW end from the cabin.

routes.name: Summit ski options
routes.description: Many summits can be reached at Kokanee Glacier Park. It is possible to ski to the top of the Pyramids, Esmeralda Peak, Cond Peak and Kokanee Peak. You can walk out onto the crest of The Battleship, but reaching the summit of The Giant's Kneecap involves some technical climbing and requires a rope.
routes.notes: Placement: no line drawn. This item lists summits reachable on skis (Pyramids, Esmeralda, Cond, Kokanee Peak; Battleship crest walkable; Giant's Kneecap needs a rope) rather than describing one descent.

routes.name: Over Easy
routes.description: Over Easy is a quick, short lap close to Kokanee Glacier Cabin that is accessed just North of the heli-pad behind Kokanee Glacier Cabin. Gain Happy Valley Ridge and skin across this small Valley towards the West end where you will see the saddle at the South end of Tanal Peak. If conditions permit and you feel comfortable ski down and find a safe place in the trees to switch as you are exposed to slides from the slope you just skied. To return to Kokanee Glacier Cabin skin Southeast up to Enterprise Pass and then descend to the Kokanee Glacier Cabin.
routes.notes: Placement: Tanal Peak (unofficial name) taken as the 2259 m DEM summit at -117.19873,49.78441, the top of the ridge running N from Enterprise Pass (ATES calls its S part 'Enterprise Ridge'); this fits the guide gains (cabin 1966 m, Big Meatballs +340) and Tanal Lake (1789 m) below its W face. Skin: cabin, heli-pad, N onto Happy Valley Ridge (~2030 m), W across Happy Valley to the subtle saddle (2091 m) at the S end of Tanal Peak. Descent: W fall line from the saddle, stopped at ~1955 m (end not given; 'a safe place in the trees'). The return skin (SE up to Enterprise Pass, 2016 m, and down to the cabin) is not drawn; it is the start of r05's skin reversed. All on MRDEM-30 (quality 3, no lidar here), so the face shape and steepness are smoothed.

routes.name: Hot Cheeks
routes.description: Hot Cheeks starts 1/3 the way up the South ridge of Tanal Peak. Beginning at Kokanee Glacier Cabin head North of the heli-pad gaining Happy Valley Ridge. Skin across Happy Valley and gain the South ridge of Tanal Peak as low as possible as Hot Cheeks is just above the North side of the saddle at the West end of Happy Valley. If conditions permit and you feel comfortable ski down and find a safe place in the trees to switch as you are exposed to slides from the slope you just skied. To return to Kokanee Glacier Cabin skin Southeast up to Enterprise Pass and then descend to the Kokanee Glacier Cabin.
routes.notes: Placement: Tanal Peak (unofficial name) taken as the 2259 m DEM summit at -117.19873,49.78441, the top of the ridge running N from Enterprise Pass (ATES calls its S part 'Enterprise Ridge'); this fits the guide gains (cabin 1966 m, Big Meatballs +340) and Tanal Lake (1789 m) below its W face. Skin: same as r01 to the saddle, then 100 m up the S ridge to ~2100 m ('just above the N side of the saddle'). Descent: W fall line, stopped at ~1960 m (end not given). Return skin to Enterprise Pass not drawn (see r05). All on MRDEM-30 (quality 3, no lidar here), so the face shape and steepness are smoothed.

routes.name: Holy Slab
routes.description: The route Holy Slab starts 1/3 the way up the South ridge and just pass Hot Cheeks on the South ridge of Tanal Peak. Starting at Kokanee Glacier Cabin head North of the heli-pad gaining Happy Valley Ridge. Skin across Happy Valley and gain the South ridge of Tanal Peak as low as possible. Climb to 2100 metres (approximately one third the way up the ridge) avoiding any cornices that may form along the ridge. Ski down the West face of Tanal Peak but be sure conditions are safe first as this face slides frequently as it is steep and sustained. Stopping at valley bottom you will be at the South end of Tanal Lake. Be sure to switch over somewhere safe as you are exposed to slides from the slope you just skied. To return to Kokanee Glacier Cabin skin Southeast up to Enterprise Pass and then descend to the Kokanee Glacier Cabin.
routes.notes: Placement: Tanal Peak (unofficial name) taken as the 2259 m DEM summit at -117.19873,49.78441, the top of the ridge running N from Enterprise Pass (ATES calls its S part 'Enterprise Ridge'); this fits the guide gains (cabin 1966 m, Big Meatballs +340) and Tanal Lake (1789 m) below its W face. Skin: same as r02, on up the S ridge crest to 2127 m. The guide's '2100 m, one third up the ridge' is only 10 m above the saddle on this DEM, so the start sits one third up (matches the 180 m gain). Descent: W face fall line to the S end of Tanal Lake. Vertical (~340 m) exceeds the 180 m gain because the lake is ~175 m below the cabin; return skin to Enterprise Pass not drawn (see r05). All on MRDEM-30 (quality 3, no lidar here), so the face shape and steepness are smoothed.

routes.name: Big Meatballs
routes.description: Big Meatballs starts at the summit of Tanal Peak and requires a sustained 340 metre climb starting at Kokanee Glacier Cabin. The easiest way to the summit is via Happy Valley Ridge which lies directly North of the cabin. Head North past the heli-pad and gaining Happy Valley Ridge and then skin across Happy Valley and gain the South ridge of Tanal Peak as low as possible. Climb this to the summit avoiding any cornices that may form. From the summit ski down the West face of Tanal Peak but be sure conditions are safe first as this face slides frequently as it is steep and sustained. Stopping at valley bottom at Tanal Lake be sure to switch over somewhere safe as you are exposed to slides from both sides of the valley. To return to Kokanee Glacier Cabin you need only to skin Southeast up to Enterprise Pass and then descend to the cabin.
routes.notes: Placement: Tanal Peak (unofficial name) taken as the 2259 m DEM summit at -117.19873,49.78441, the top of the ridge running N from Enterprise Pass (ATES calls its S part 'Enterprise Ridge'); this fits the guide gains (cabin 1966 m, Big Meatballs +340) and Tanal Lake (1789 m) below its W face. Skin: same as r03, on up the S ridge crest to the summit (~18 deg max on the DEM; keep off cornices). Descent: SW down the W face fall line to the S end of Tanal Lake. Vertical (~470 m) exceeds the 340 m gain because the lake is below the cabin; return skin not drawn (see r05). All on MRDEM-30 (quality 3, no lidar here), so the face shape and steepness are smoothed.

routes.name: Future Champion
routes.description: Future Champions is found on the far North end of the West side of Tanal Peak and in order to avoid climbing up and over Tanal Peak and the exposure that this presents, the best way to reach this route is to descend Enterprise pass and climb the West ridge of Tanal Peak which is less steep and open. Enterprise Pass is a short 60 metre climb directly north of the Kokanee Glacier Cabin heli pad. Ski down into the valley and cross Tanal Lake being sure to avoid avalanche exposure from both sides. From the lake contour north and then East to gain the West ridge of Tanal Peak. Climb until you reach 2100 metres then switch over to ski mode and ski directly down to Tanal Lake staying in the relative safety of the trees. From valley bottom skin back up to Enterprise Pass (to the Southeast) and back to the cabin the exact same way you came.
routes.notes: Placement: Tanal Peak (unofficial name) taken as the 2259 m DEM summit at -117.19873,49.78441, the top of the ridge running N from Enterprise Pass (ATES calls its S part 'Enterprise Ridge'); this fits the guide gains (cabin 1966 m, Big Meatballs +340) and Tanal Lake (1789 m) below its W face. 'West ridge' taken as the W spur from the summit (crest 1850 m at its W toe to 2101 m at -117.20353,49.78474). Skin: cabin, heli-pad, Enterprise Pass (2016 m, ~50 m above the cabin), down the valley N to the S end of Tanal Lake, across the lake, N along the shore, then E onto the spur (least-slope path) and up its crest to 2100 m (crest is ~25 deg in places). Return is the same line reversed. Descent: S/SW fall line off the spur to Tanal Lake (~310 m). All on MRDEM-30 (quality 3, no lidar here), so the face shape and steepness are smoothed.

routes.name: Cream Puff
routes.description: Cream Puff is also found on the far North end of the West side of Tanal Peak so again in order to avoid climbing up and over Tanal Peak follow the same up track as you would for Future Champion above. Descend Enterprise pass and climb the West ridge of Tanal Peak which is less steep and open than Tanal Peak. Enterprise Pass is a short 60 metre climb directly north of the Kokanee Glacier Cabin heli pad. Ski down into the valley and cross Tanal Lake being sure to avoid avalanche exposure from both sides. From the lake contour north and then East to gain the West ridge of Tanal Peak. Climb until you reach 2100 metres then switch over to ski mode and ski down in a Northwesterly direction into the trees for approximately 140 metres of gentle turns. Once the terrain mellows out you will need to skin West to then wrap back around to the South and again reach Tanal Lake. From here skin back up to Enterprise Pass and back to the cabin the exact same way you came in.
routes.notes: Placement: Tanal Peak (unofficial name) taken as the 2259 m DEM summit at -117.19873,49.78441, the top of the ridge running N from Enterprise Pass (ATES calls its S part 'Enterprise Ridge'); this fits the guide gains (cabin 1966 m, Big Meatballs +340) and Tanal Lake (1789 m) below its W face. Skin: identical to r05 (same up-track to 2100 m on the W spur). Descent: NW off the spur for the guide's ~140 m of gentle turns, ending ~1960 m; descent_m set to 140 from the text. The exit (skin W, then wrap S back to Tanal Lake, then r05's line back to the cabin) is not drawn. All on MRDEM-30 (quality 3, no lidar here), so the face shape and steepness are smoothed.

pois.description: Cabin heli-pad, just NW of Kokanee Glacier Cabin (position approximate).
